newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cypriots to hold Greek Cypriot for eight days.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriots to hold Greek Cypriot for eight days.

text.p: A Turkish Cypriot military court on Tuesday remanded a Greek Cypriot in custody for eight days after he crossed into Turkish-controlled northern Cyprus at the weekend, witnesses said.
Military judge Yasar Atasagun said that eight days was needed for an investigation into how he crossed into the northern part of the island.

Turkish Cypriot police arrested Savvas Siderenou, aged 22, on Saturday night after he crossed the "green line" that divides the Greek and Turkish communities on the island near the village of Achna close to a British military base.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia backed by the military ruling in Athens at the time.

The international community, with the exception of Turkey, recognises the Greek Cypriot administration in the south as the only government on the island. The Turkish Cypriot breakaway administration in the north is only recognised by Turkey.
